messages.subject: Re: How to share methylkit objects
messages.body_plain:
Hi, to share a methylBaseDB object you have to copy the underlying tabix file. If you are using methylKit version 1.13.1 or above, the tabix file should include a header and can be loaded again using the readMethylDB function.
Please see here for details: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/methylKit/inst/doc/methylKit.html#53_Loading_methylDB_objects_from_tabix_files

messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] Re: Heatmap of DMRs in methylKit
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
You can try to look at the script on this link:
 https://github.com/exa564/HSCe_Aging

Essentially you have to save a bed file with your DMCs (3 columns: chr start end), a file with your DMRs and a perc.meth.txt file with percent methylation for each sample for each CpG.
You can get and save a txt from your perc.meth file after performing the unite on methylkit:
meth=unite(norm_myobj, destrand=TRUE)
perc.meth <- percMethylation(meth, rowids = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: How to share methylkit objects
messages.body_plain:
Hi, the tabix file you should download has the "txt.bgz" extension. You can easily find the underlying tabix file for an object by using the getDBPath() function which prints the absolute location of the file.

The makeMethylDB function is used to "save" a normal in-memory methylKit object into a database methylKitDB object. In the vignette it is used to create some example tabix file and show the corresponding header.
